pages.quiz:
INTEGRATED SCIENCE — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #2
====

GRADE: Grade 7
SUBJECT: INTEGRATED SCIENCE
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Diffusion is best described as: (1 mark)
   A. A chemical reaction forming ash
   B. Heating until a solid melts
   C. Movement of water only across a membrane
   D. Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. In a food chain, green plants are usually: (1 mark)
   A. Tertiary consumers
   B. Producers
   C. Primary consumers only
   D. Decomposers only

3. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Electrical Energy? (1 mark)
   A. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Electrical Energy.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Electrical Energy.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Electrical Energy.

4. An element is: (1 mark)
   A. A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means
   B. A mixture of two liquids
   C. Any substance that conducts electricity
   D. Any white crystal used in cooking

5. Boiling point of pure water at standard pressure is about: (1 mark)
   A. 37 °C
   B. 50 °C
   C. 0 °C
   D. 100 °C

6. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory Safety? (1 mark)
   A. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory Safety.
   B. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory Safety.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory Safety.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory Safety.

7. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Magnetism? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Magnetism.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Magnetism.
   C. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Magnetism.
   D. Guess results without recording observations on Magnetism.

8. Why is water unsuitable for a petrol fire? (1 mark)
   A. Petrol fires have no fuel
   B. Water always increases oxygen
   C. Water removes heat too quickly
   D. Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

9. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Laboratory apparatus and instruments? (1 mark)
   A. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   B. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Laboratory apparatus and instruments.
   D. Skip labelling diagrams related to Laboratory apparatus and instruments.

10. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Mixtures? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Mixtures.
   B. Guess results without recording observations on Mixtures.
   C. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures.
   D. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Mixtures.

11. A compound differs from a mixture because: (1 mark)
   A. Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio
   B. A mixture always has a fixed melting point
   C. Mixtures cannot exist in Kenya
   D. A compound can be separated by filtering only

12. Which practice best shows correct science when studying Human Reproductive System? (1 mark)
   A. Skip labelling diagrams related to Human Reproductive System.
   B. Taste unknown substances to “learn faster” about Human Reproductive System.
   C. Guess results without recording observations on Human Reproductive System.
   D. Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproductive System.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Electrical Energy and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Magnetism and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Introduction to Integrated Science and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Laboratory Safety and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. D — Net movement of particles from high to low concentration

2. B — Producers

3. A — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Electrical Energy.

4. A — A pure substance that cannot be broken down into a simpler substance by chemical means

5. D — 100 °C

6. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory Safety.

7. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Magnetism.

8. D — Water can spread burning petrol instead of putting it out safely

9. B — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Laboratory apparatus and instruments.

10. C — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Mixtures.

11. A — Elements in a compound are chemically combined in a fixed ratio

12. D — Observe carefully, use correct terms, and follow safety rules for Human Reproductive System.

13. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Electrical Energy; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

14. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Magnetism; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

15. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Introduction to Integrated Science; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

16. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Laboratory Safety; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
